_comment: Patch notes for the website and releases. Maintained by etl/changelog.py; add notes for the next release under 'unreleased'.

website: Objects with the same name (e.g. every Campfire or Mailbox) are one entry in the object list; its page shows all of them on the map, and Quick facts lists the object IDs on the selected map.
Maps on quest, object, NPC and item pages can be zoomed out to show the whole map again.
Pages note when a translated text comes from AzerothCore (Wrath of the Lich King), since it may differ from Classic.

Lua exports of texts follow a locale-file layout with English as fallback: the enUS file creates the table, other languages only replace the entries they translate, and objectives are one text with $B line breaks.
The Lua export page no longer offers the References and Format options: exports always use plain IDs and the addon format.
In the Lua export, startedBy is grouped by kind, e.g. { npc = {196}, item = {1307} }, so quest starters of different kinds can be told apart.
The site now covers WoW Forever only: the Classic Era version and the version switch are gone, and addresses are shorter (e.g. #/quest/2); old links still work.
data: Missing translations are now filled in from AzerothCore as a last resort, for example about 3,800 quest completion texts in Latin American Spanish and many NPC and object names.
Classic Era data and maps are no longer built or published.

website: Every field on the Lua export page has an ⓘ explaining what it contains and how it appears in the Lua file.
The site no longer scrolls sideways on phones: the menu wraps onto a second line and the export form fits the screen.
In the Lua export the quest fields starters and enders are now called startedBy and finishedBy, matching QuestieDB.
The database is also online at data.morthen.net, updated after every data release.
Vendor lists show limited stock (e.g. "limited: 2, restocks every 2 h"), and entries known only from VMangos carry a VMangos badge with a note that they may be outdated.
Item pages have a map showing where the item is sold, dropped or looted, with a colour for each kind of source.
Map labels (zone, town and region names) are now in English.
Dungeon and raid pages show the instance map: one row of tabs picks the floor, a second row the outdoor maps with the quest givers.
Maps can no longer be zoomed out beyond the map itself, zoom in further and in finer steps, and a zone page always shows the zone's own map first.
In the Lua export the player's name placeholder $N is now written as ${playerName}.
dataNotes: Quest texts that QuestieDB, VMangos and the game cache lack can now be filled in from Wowhead in every language; quests using them list Wowhead as a source.
NPCs, objects and items that have no name in QuestieDB use the VMangos name or are shown as e.g. "NPC #214954" instead of breaking the update.
Vendors now also come from the VMangos server database, adding about 1,600 vendor entries; these may be outdated, especially for WoW Forever.
About 3,000 more WoW Forever quest texts from Wowhead across all languages; Russian texts no longer contain the race or character name of whoever recorded them.

classic: 25 quests updated (texts, objectives, rewards or chains), e.g. A Fair Trade, Arrows Are For Sissies, Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe, Cyclonian, Gathering the Cure, Gathering the Cure, Gyro... What?, The Touch of Zanzil.
forever: 175 quests updated (texts, objectives, rewards or chains), e.g. Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe, Cyclonian, Desperate Prayer, Earth Sapta, Earth Sapta, Fire Sapta, Gyro... What?, The Touch of Zanzil.
Quest descriptions: English +1, German +5, Spanish (EU) +4, Spanish (LA) +5, French +5, Korean +189, Portuguese +2,753, Russian +4, Chinese (simplified) +4, Chinese (traditional) +1,425.

website: The docker-compose.yml of each release pulls the image from Docker Hub (derskunky/wow-quest-database); the image files attached to the release carry the same name.
The Lua export page separates data fields from localization fields, each with All/None, so you can export only the data file or only the language files.

The export page is now grouped into Selection, Data file and Localization files, starts with everything ticked, disables export when nothing is selected, and keeps both field choices in the page link.

Every quest with a zone now has a map ID (uiMapId) for the in-game map API: 3,246 of 3,261 in Classic Era and 3,592 of 3,757 in WoW Forever.

website: First version of the WoW Quest Database for Classic Era and WoW Forever: quests, NPCs, objects and items with detail pages, a quest list with filters and a global search.
Quest pages show objectives, descriptions, rewards and quest chains, with an interactive map of quest givers, turn-ins and objective locations.
Map images from the game clients for both versions, fully explored or with fog of war.
Questlines as a graph in the style of BtWQuests, with faction and class filters and progress tracking in the browser.
Quest texts and names in ten languages.
Lua export of all data, on the website and as a command-line tool, with texts in separate files per language.
Filters are kept in the address, so going back returns to the same view.
Docker image for self-hosting, released automatically when the data changes.
dataNotes: Initial data from QuestieDB combined with the VMangos world database: 4,257 quests in Classic Era and 4,989 in WoW Forever, plus NPCs, objects and items.
The Zephras Isle storyline (Skyborne starting zone in WoW Forever) as a questline, based on warcraft.wiki.gg.
Item rewards of Forever quests taken from QuestRewards.lua.
